note: Private campground (est. 1999) on about 18 acres along the Cedar River in Charles City, with a 3-acre fishing pond (boat dock, small beach). Areas on the operator's map: Northwest Territory, Midlands, the ADA area and Outback, a row of OB pull-throughs on the road between the pond and the river, and Blackbird Island along the river; canoe launch ramp, on the paved walk/bike trail, near the HyVee. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the operator's site: $30 electric / $40 full hookup (rates page updated 2025-12-01; monthly $600 summer / $750 winter now in fees.note), water+sewer at full-hookup sites, open year-round; added showers/dump/laundry from the map and phone/email reservations with self-registration. 50-amp and 50-ft rig figures not stated by the operator (left as derived). Waterfront 'not waterfront' looks wrong: lead below.
flags: PRIVATE GATES: posted rate $30-40 (2025-12 rates page) under the US$50 gate; no gateway within 40 km (St. Paul 213 km). PRESENCE: working operator website with phone 641-257-0549 (matches Google). Google Maps 4.7 stars / 191 reviews; RV Life 4.5 stars / 5 reviews ($$, avg $28); Good Sam Park per the directory, and a Sept 2025 RV Life reviewer paid $30 'discount Good Sam'. No review site under 4.0 with 25+ reviews. Pass.

LONG-STAY: not mostly seasonal on what I read. Nightly rates lead the rates page, monthly beside them ($600 Apr-Oct, $750 Nov-Mar). Reviews are mostly overnight/short stays (Google: 'Looking for an overnight campground while driving through Iowa', 3 months ago; 'attending the wedding', 4 months ago; RV Life: 'Quiet One Night Stay', 9/2025); one RV Life reviewer 'stayed for multiple months for work' (9/2025). Summer imagery shows the Northwest Territory loop by the office densely filled (~40 rigs), which may be the monthly area; the river and pond rows were mostly empty. Five tests: 1 seasonal-only sites not stated; 2 nightly rate posted; 3 no homes/lots for sale seen; 4 nightly sites plainly more than 1 in 10; 5 no approval rule. Pass.

WATERFRONT RE-AUDIT LEAD (up): stored 'not waterfront' rests on 'pads set back from the Cedar River and pond behind a continuous ~100m treeline', which describes the pin (the office/Northwest Territory loop, ~300 m from the river), not the river rows. The operator's map puts the OB row on the river side of the road between the pond and the Cedar, and imagery (43.0566,-92.6655, 110 m) shows those angled pull-through pads backing onto the river bank: the western pads ~5-15 m from the water behind a fringe of scattered bank trees, the eastern pads ~20-25 m from it across open grass at the canoe-launch point. The Cedar here is ~100 m wide (riverfront scale). Reviews: RV Life 9/2026 motorhome at site OB1 'I was able to look out my front window and have a beautiful view of a river'; RV Life 6/2026 site OB5 and Google (4 months ago) 'Right on the river, very beautiful and quiet!'. Reads as riverfront for the OB river row (at least riverview); the open point may be the canoe-launch day-use spot, so judge from the western pads. The 3-acre pond is under 5 acres and carries no value.

UNVERIFIED: hookups.electric 50 and sites.max_rig_ft 50 came from the old note prose; the operator's pages state neither (no amperage, no lengths). Left as derived; not cleared because their original source is unknown.

PIN: stored 43.05870,-92.66270 is at the office / Northwest Territory loop (Google 43.05854,-92.66262); the sites spread ~400 m SW to the pond and river rows. Within the 250 m line of the main loop; no change needed.
